title: TSM Stock Eyes $500 Despite Asian Chip Pullback as TSMC Expands U.S. Manufacturing Ambitions - FXLeaders
content: TSM stock reached a fresh record above $487 as Nvidia demand and Elon Musk’s TeraFab discussions boosted sentiment, but the retreat toward $470 highlights the risks facing an increasingly expensive semiconductor rally. TSM stock climbed above $487 on Monday, extending its powerful uptrend before retreating toward $470 in today’s session. The record move followed stronger semiconductor sentiment after Nvidia’s latest earnings and renewed attention on potential cooperation between Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company and Elon Musk’s companies. Musk confirmed discussions with TSMC regarding the proposed TeraFab semiconductor project. The talks remain preliminary, leaving the final structure uncertain, but the project could involve manufacturing custom chips for Tesla, SpaceX and xAI as computing requirements continue to expand. TSMC could potentially operate a Texas facility or provide manufacturing technology for TeraFab, while Musk’s companies could retain control of the venture. The potential project adds another growth opportunity for TSMC as demand for advanced chips expands. However, any new manufacturing investment would require substantial capital and could add to the cost pressures associated with building semiconductor capacity in the United States. TSMC is also reportedly considering a major semiconductor manufacturing campus in Texas. Discussions remain preliminary, but a large-scale Texas expansion would complement the company’s massive investment in Arizona. TSMC has previously committed $65 billion to three Arizona fabrication facilities, while further expansion plans could eventually create a much larger U.S. manufacturing ecosystem. The strategy could bring production closer to major American technology customers and reduce some geographic concentration risks. However, overseas fabs are more expensive to build and operate, potentially putting pressure on margins during the construction and ramp-up phases. TSM stock was already showing strong momentum before NVIDIA released its results and the TeraFab talks gave it another boos, and the move above $487 suggests investors are increasingly positioning for continued growth in advanced semiconductor demand. The company’s manufacturing leadership gives it a central role in the production of high-end chips used by major technology companies. If NVIDIA continues increasing output to meet growing demand for advanced computing systems, TSMC could remain one of the major beneficiaries because higher chip volumes require additional leading-edge manufacturing capacity. NVIDIA’s forecast for another major increase in quarterly revenue strengthens the argument that the current spending cycle has not yet ended. Nvidia remains one of the most important demand drivers for TSMC. Nvidia designs its advanced processors but relies on external foundries to manufacture its leading-edge chips, with TSMC playing a central role in that supply chain. As Nvidia increases production of increasingly powerful processors, demand for TSMC’s advanced manufacturing capacity could remain strong. This creates an important distinction between the two companies. Nvidia must meet extremely high growth expectations, while TSMC can potentially benefit from rising demand across multiple semiconductor customers. The semiconductor industry is undergoing a massive investment cycle, with technology companies spending heavily on computing infrastructure and advanced chips. For TSMC, this supports revenue growth but also raises expectations. A slowdown in Nvidia or broader infrastructure spending could eventually reduce orders across the supply chain, while excessive capacity could become a longer-term risk if demand fails to keep pace. For now, $487 marks the latest record high, while the retreat toward $470 shows that buyers still need to defend the breakout. A move toward $500 would extend the bullish momentum, but elevated valuations and enormous industry spending requirements could make the next leg of the rally more difficult to sustain.

Shares of Microsoft (MSFT), Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL), Amazon (AMZN) and Oracle Corp. (ORCL) were in focus on Friday after the U.K. government designated the four companies as Critical Third Parties (CTPs) to strengthen and safeguard the country’s financial systems. At the time of writing, MSFT stock was up 0.4%, ORCL shares climbed 1%, while GOOG and AMZN shares edged 0.2% lower each. The firms covered under the new framework are Microsoft Ireland Operations, Google Cloud EMEA, Amazon Web Services EMEA, and Oracle Corporation UK. Bank of England, the Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA), and the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) will jointly oversee the critical services the four companies provide to the financial sector. The aim is to reduce the risk of widespread disruption if a major cloud provider experiences operational issues. Regulatory oversight will apply only to the financial sector, not to their broader business operations. The designated companies will be required to maintain strong systems to identify, manage, and recover from disruptions affecting services used by financial institutions. Regulators will also be allowed to gather information, assess operational resilience, and, when necessary, introduce or enforce CTP-specific rules to ensure the continuity of critical services. “These designations will help ensure the critical services financial firms rely on remain resilient, protecting consumers and businesses while supporting growth across the economy,” said Rachel Blake, Economic Secretary to the Treasury of the United Kingdom. The Critical Third Parties designation was established under the UK’s Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 to improve operational resilience after growing concerns that disruptions at major cloud providers could affect multiple financial institutions simultaneously. The framework builds on the Bank of England’s 2021 assessment that the financial sector’s increasing reliance on a small number of cloud providers warranted stronger regulatory oversight to safeguard essential financial services relied upon by millions of consumers and businesses. According to a CloudGuard Financial Services Threat Report published earlier this year, cyber risks faced by the U.K.’s financial sector have reached a record high, with the industry accounting for about 28% of all cyberattacks in the country. The report highlighted growing threats from ransomware, nation-state hackers, and AI-powered scams such as deepfakes and targeted phishing. It also warned of a sharp rise in credential theft, with billions of stolen login credentials circulating on the dark web. AppLovin (APP) shares hit a fresh 52-week low and closed down about 4.5% on Wednesday after Wells Fargo told clients a recent spike in merchant Pixel installs looks weaker than the raw count suggests, pushing back on the idea that e-commerce customer growth had suddenly accelerated. A Pixel is a small tracking tag a retailer puts on its website. On Shopify, AppLovin’s free app can install it automatically and sync the product catalog. Pixel tallies have been one of the few public proxies for whether the June launch is landing real stores. Wells said investors had called about a jump in Pixel adds over the past two weeks. Raw installs did rise. The mix did not, the firm argued. Most of the new sites were Asia-Pacific Shopify storefronts with little or no measurable web traffic. The share of new Pixel sites with no traffic began climbing in June and reached about 85% in the latest two weeks, up from about 30% before June, the firm said. (TSLA) heads into next week's second-quarter (Q2) earnings with growing pressure from its retail investor base, as Robotaxi delays, missed milestones, and the Optimus production ramp dominate shareholder questions. TSLA stock is down 3% so far this week, with shares also down 0.3% in premarket trading on Thursday. Robotaxi is by far the dominant theme among the highest-ranked retail questions. The EV giant is expected to report its Q2 results on July 22. One of the most-upvoted submissions asks why Tesla has repeatedly missed its own autonomy targets: "Tesla has missed short term guidance on robotaxi 3 earnings reports in a row... What is keeping Tesla back from accomplishing these short term goals that they've set for themselves?" Another asks: "Why has growth of robotaxi vehicles stalled? When will we see Cybercab start customer rides?" Investors are also demanding concrete operating metrics, including fleet size, paid rides, intervention rates, cost per mile and revenue contribution, instead of broader progress updates. Others want revised rollout milestones after earlier targets were missed. Musk said in 2019 that Tesla could have one million Robotaxis on the road by the end of 2020, a target that never materialized as Full Self-Driving (FSD) remained a supervised system. Tesla reset expectations during its October 2024 Cybercab unveiling, targeting unsupervised Robotaxi operations in Texas and California in 2025 and volume production of Cybercabs in 2026. The company launched a limited paid Robotaxi service in Austin in June 2025 before beginning production of Cybercab earlier this year, though Musk cautioned that the initial production ramp would be "agonizingly slow." Optimus was the second most-discussed topic, with shareholders seeking updates on Gen 3 production, factory deployment and commercial rollout. The highest-ranked Optimus question asks about the Gen 3 production ramp, initial factory deployment and external sales timeline for 2027. Others ask how many Optimus robots are currently working inside Tesla factories, what tasks they perform and what manufacturing bottlenecks still stand in the way of mass production. The questions mirror Robotaxi concerns. Tesla first targeted limited Optimus production in 2023 before shifting toward low-rate production and internal factory deployment through 2026. Musk has said that the ramp for Optimus is also "agonizingly slow," arguing that nearly every component is new. Koyfin estimates call for Q2 revenue of $26.29 billion, up 17% from a year ago. To place an order, customers can browse the Retail or Electronics category in the Uber Eats app, search for GameStop, select their items, and choose a delivery time. Once the order is placed, customers can then track it in real time, similar to restaurant deliveries. GameStop is the latest retailer to join Uber Eats as the company continues expanding beyond restaurant deliveries. title: Gateside By TSA PreCheck Brings Back A Piece Of Airport Goodbyes At Billings Logan - Mix 97.1
content: Not to sound like grandad telling you a tale about the "good old days," but way back in the pre-2001 times, going to the airport was a much different experience. Pre-9/11, there was no such thing as the TSA. Anyone, with or without a ticket, could basically walk right up to the gates. If your loved one was jetting off for work, vacation, or whatever, you could hang out at the gate as long as you'd like. Read More: Chain Stores and Restaurants Closing Locations in 2026 Perhaps you'd sit in the concourse and watch their plane take off, lingering long after the "final call for boarding" went over the loudspeakers. On the flip side, you could be right there waiting for them at the gate when they came home, instead of crowding around the baggage claim. Of course, the world will never return to what is what like before September 11, 2001, but things are getting just a tad friendlier at airports across the United States, including Billings Logan International. The TSA is rolling out the Gateside PreCheck service. According to a 10/6 press release from BIL, the program will allow qualified individuals without boarding passes to be screened and go beyond the TSA passenger screening checkpoint. “The Gateside by TSA PreCheck program is a welcome addition to the airport experience at BIL,” said Jeff Roach, Director of Aviation and Transit, “you can now go to the gate to see travelers off, greet arriving passengers, or just to experience post-security amenities at the airport.” The program only allows 50 people per day beyond the TSA security gates at BIL. You can participate anytime the TSA gates are staffed, and you must leave the concourse before 8 PM. Individuals will need to pre-register with TSA at least 24 hours in advance, but not more than three days ahead. You can do that HERE. I like this program a lot. The days of sitting by yourself for two hours before your flight can now be a thing of the past.

title: Elon Musk’s Terafab Discussions Send Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) to Record High - Blockonomi
content: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM) shares touched unprecedented territory Monday as the semiconductor giant continued its impressive 2026 performance. The stock advanced as much as 2.75%, cementing its position among this year’s top-performing chipmakers. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited, TSM The rally gained momentum after Elon Musk publicly acknowledged preliminary negotiations with TSMC concerning a potential collaboration on his ambitious Terafab venture. The project envisions a large-scale semiconductor manufacturing facility in Texas designed to meet the chip requirements of Tesla, SpaceX, and xAI. Technology reporter Tim Culpan disclosed that TSMC is examining potential strategies to assist the emerging chipmaker in operating its planned Texas production sites. Musk addressed the reports on X, stating “Just discussions, but something may come of it.” Intel’s shares experienced a contrasting fate, falling more than 2% despite the company’s April partnership announcement with Terafab. Market participants questioned the implications of potential TSMC involvement for Intel’s foundry strategy. Bloomberg revealed Thursday that TSMC is simultaneously evaluating an independent manufacturing complex in Texas. The prospective development could require investments reaching tens of billions of dollars across multiple production facilities, though negotiations remain in preliminary stages. Individual fabrication plants are anticipated to require investments of at least $20 billion each. The ultimate green light may depend on whether Congress extends the 35% advanced-manufacturing tax credit beyond its current December 2026 expiration. North American clients currently represent over 75% of TSMC’s wafer sales. Technology leaders including Nvidia and AMD rank among the company’s largest customers for cutting-edge chip production services. Deputy Co-Chief Operating Officer Cliff Hou disclosed that TSMC has approximately doubled its equipment procurement budget within the last twelve months. The expansion addresses explosive growth in AI infrastructure requirements. TSMC has pledged $265 billion toward its Arizona manufacturing footprint. Additional international initiatives are underway in Japan and Germany, with exploratory discussions happening in Singapore. Industry analyst Counterpoint Research identifies TSMC as the “central beneficiary” of artificial intelligence semiconductor expansion. The research firm highlighted second-quarter revenue climbing 34% year-over-year to $40.2 billion. TSMC’s Foundry 2.0 market position expanded to approximately 42%, compared with 38% in 2025. Counterpoint forecasts full-year 2026 revenue growth near 43%, with momentum building toward 50% expansion in the latter half. S&P Global Ratings projects hyperscaler artificial intelligence expenditures will reach $1.5 trillion by 2028. The ratings agency views TSMC as relatively insulated should that investment eventually moderate. S&P attributed TSMC’s resilience to its technological advantage and broad customer portfolio, which should preserve pricing power and margin stability. The firm anticipates profitability and cash flow will remain above 2026 benchmarks even amid softening demand scenarios. While pursuing global expansion, TSMC maintains its position that cutting-edge manufacturing processes will remain concentrated in Taiwan. Company representatives declined to address the Texas campus speculation, responding only, “We have no comment on market rumors.” TSMC’s October 15 earnings release carries significant weight on Wall Street. Consensus estimates call for EPS of $4.45, up substantially from $2.92 twelve months prior, with revenue anticipated at $45.54 billion versus $33.10 billion last year. The equity currently commands a price-to-earnings multiple around 35.3. Analyst consensus favors a Buy rating with a mean price target of $547.38, supported by recent Buy or Outperform recommendations from Stifel, Bernstein, and Needham. title: Major Banks | BofA Securities: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM.US) maintains ties with "Musk's dynamic duo"; likelihood of sharing technology or control with Terafab remains low - 富途牛牛
content: Bank of America Securities released a research report stating that Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM.US) maintains strong relationships with customers associated with Elon Musk. It expects that, as Tesla (TSLA.US) and SpaceX (SPCX.US) expand their businesses, cooperation between the two sides will deepen. However, the likelihood of Taiwan Semiconductor licensing technology to Terafab or jointly operating a fab with Terafab while holding a significant equity stake is relatively low. The bank noted that on Saturday last week (the 3rd), when responding to reports about a potential manufacturing partnership between Taiwan Semiconductor and Terafab, Musk said, "It's just discussions, but there could be results." According to the bank's estimates, Tesla and SpaceX—directly (in automotive/robotics and cloud‑based AI ASICs) and indirectly (through commercial HPC chips such as GPUs and network switches)—account for roughly 2% to 3% of Taiwan Semiconductor's sales. Customer neutrality is at the heart of Taiwan Semiconductor's foundry model; its joint-venture fabs have a limited track record and mostly employ mature processes. Even for Apple (AAPL.US), which contributed roughly 21% of its revenue from 2015 to 2025 and primarily uses advanced processes, Taiwan Semiconductor does not co‑own any fabs, in order to maintain full operational control and customer neutrality. The firm further noted that, according to Terafab's application for the JETI project in Texas, the four-phase plan from 2026 to 2036 will involve approximately US$119 billion in investment, with about 60% allocated to equipment procurement. Spending from 2026 to 2028 will be heavily weighted toward facility construction, while from 2029 to 2036 annual equipment expenditures are expected to range between US$6 billion and US$8 billion. According to the firm's estimates, expanding advanced‑process capacity by 1,000 wafers per month in the U.S. would require more than US$600 million; even if the technology roadmap proceeds smoothly, Terafab could add at most around 10,000 wafers per month annually, making it difficult to achieve economies of scale. As a result, Taiwan Semiconductor will likely remain Tesla and SpaceX's primary foundry partner. The firm reiterated its "Buy" rating on Taiwan Semiconductor (2330.TW), assigning a 2027 projected price-to-earnings ratio of 20x (currently around 16x) and maintaining a target price of NT$3,100, believing that the stock is in the mid-cycle phase, supported by robust AI demand pipelines. Federal energy officials announced a conditional $4.2 billion loan commitment Monday to modernize and boost power production across nuclear generation facilities in Pennsylvania and Ohio, targeting rising regional electricity costs and surging energy demand. The funding, extended by the U.S. Department of Energy’s Office of Energy Dominance Financing to Texas-based utility operator Vistra (VST), aims to expand generation capacity across existing facilities without necessitating new power transmission infrastructure. According to department officials, the initiative supports executive measures to bolster domestic nuclear infrastructure and restore American energy output. The planned upgrades focus on Vistra’s Beaver Valley plant in Pennsylvania, along with the Davis-Besse and Perry facilities in Ohio. By executing thermodynamic and hardware uprates, the project will add 433 megawatts of power capacity while maintaining nearly 4 gigawatts of steady baseload electricity—enough to supply power to more than 3 million households. Beyond expanding immediate output, the modernization strategy will help extend operational life cycles at the three Midwestern plants by up to 20 years beyond their current licensing terms. The conditional loan arrangement also leaves open an option to fund future uprates at Vistra’s Comanche Peak facility in Texas. Construction, engineering, and specialized maintenance during scheduled outage periods are projected to support about 3,000 temporary jobs while protecting thousands of permanent operational positions at the facilities. By boosting generation within established facility footprints, the funding addresses growing power consumption across the 13-state PJM Interconnection grid, which serves major industrial and residential centers throughout the Mid-Atlantic and Midwest regions. title: New Record in TSM Stock, Eyeing $500 as TSMC Explores Role in Musk TeraFab - FXLeaders
content: TSM stock has climbed to fresh record highs above $480 as strong NVIDIA results reinforce semiconductor demand and potential TSMC involvement in Elon Musk’s TeraFab adds another growth catalyst. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing shares have extended their rally above $480, surpassing the previous record from June and moving toward the psychologically important $500 level. The latest momentum comes as investors assess the potential for TSMC to participate in Elon Musk’s $16.8 billion TeraFab project in Texas. Musk has confirmed that discussions with TSMC are underway, although he indicated that negotiations remain at an early stage. Intel was previously identified as a manufacturing partner after joining the project in April, with its 14A process technology selected for the proposed facility. However, reports that TSMC is exploring a role could create an additional opportunity for the world’s largest advanced-chip foundry. The potential partnership follows reports that TSMC is considering expanding its manufacturing presence in Texas after developing its Arizona operations. Reports have suggested TSMC could eventually establish multiple advanced fabs in Texas. One possibility would involve TSMC owning and operating a new facility while SpaceX participates through equity investment or guaranteed purchase agreements. The TeraFab concept was initially proposed by Musk in 2025 after he argued that existing semiconductor supply would not be sufficient for Tesla’s long-term requirements. In March 2026, Musk announced plans for a semiconductor facility in Austin, Texas, positioned near Tesla’s headquarters and intended as a joint venture between Tesla and SpaceX. Intel subsequently joined the project, but the potential involvement of TSMC could broaden the manufacturing strategy. NVIDIA’s latest results provide another major catalyst for TSM stock. NVIDIA operates a fabless model, designing its processors while relying on external manufacturers such as TSMC for production. TSMC manufactures the majority of NVIDIA’s most advanced chips, meaning continued growth in GPU demand directly supports demand for TSMC’s leading-edge manufacturing capacity. Strong NVIDIA revenue and expectations for continued infrastructure spending therefore reinforce the broader semiconductor cycle. Unlike NVIDIA, which must justify extremely high growth expectations, TSMC can benefit from demand generated by multiple customers across the semiconductor industry. TSM stock was already showing strong momentum before NVIDIA released its results, and the move above $487 suggests investors are increasingly positioning for continued growth in advanced semiconductor demand. The company’s manufacturing leadership gives it a central role in the production of high-end chips used by major technology companies. The same spending boom supporting TSM stock also creates longer-term risks. Semiconductor companies are committing enormous amounts of capital to computing infrastructure, advanced processors and new manufacturing facilities. For TSMC, this creates opportunities for higher revenue and utilization, but expectations are becoming increasingly elevated. If NVIDIA’s growth slows or customers reduce infrastructure spending, semiconductor orders could eventually weaken. There is also a risk that aggressive investment creates excess capacity if supply expands faster than underlying demand. For now, buyers remain firmly in control as TSM stock trades above $480 and approaches the $500 psychological level. A sustained breakout above $500 could reinforce the broader uptrend, while failure to hold the new record zone could trigger profit-taking. With potential TeraFab involvement and strong NVIDIA-driven demand supporting the story, TSMC remains positioned to benefit from the semiconductor investment cycle. However, the increasingly aggressive spending environment means investors will need to watch both demand growth and capacity expansion closely.

title: New global standard looms: PH miners weigh costs, compliance after years of TSM investment - Bilyonaryo Business
content: Philippine mining companies are assessing the potential cost of a new global responsible-mining standard and whether years of investment in existing sustainability systems would carry over under any future shift. The Chamber of Mines of the Philippines (COMP) will convene industry executives on Oct. 26 to discuss the Consolidated Mining Standard Initiative (CMSI), which aims to bring major existing sustainability frameworks under a common global standard. “CMSI represents an important development in the evolution of responsible mining standards internationally. It seeks to bring together major existing industry sustainability frameworks and establish a more coherent global approach to responsible mining performance,” COMP chairman Michael Toledo said in an Oct. 5 letter to members. “For Philippine mining companies, it is important to understand what this development could mean for us.” At issue is how CMSI would treat investments already made under Towards Sustainable Mining (TSM), the framework currently used by COMP members. Philippine miners completed their first full cycle of TSM external verification covering 2023 to 2025, while the protocols have recently been revised to better reflect local operating conditions. The industry is seeking clarity on whether that work would be recognized under any future transition, as well as on CMSI’s governance and assurance requirements, mine-site reporting rules and treatment of different national regulatory and operating environments. COMP is also assessing the potential impact on staffing, resources and other organizational requirements, and what the standard could mean for expectations from investors, international customers and financial institutions. “We believe these are matters that merit the attention not only of sustainability professionals but also of company heads and senior management, given their potential strategic, operational and financial implications,” Toledo said. COMP stressed that it has made no decision to replace TSM. “At this stage, therefore, your Chamber is not approaching CMSI as a decision to transition from TSM,” Toledo said. “Rather, we believe that our members should have the opportunity to hear directly from MAC about CMSI, understand its potential implications, and assess what it could mean for their companies and for Philippine mining as a whole.” Mining Association of Canada President Pierre Gratton will brief Philippine companies on CMSI’s direction, governance and implementation at the Manila meeting.

content: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Ltd. TSM is doubling down on the artificial intelligence semiconductor boom as surging demand pushes the chipmaker to expand manufacturing and advanced-packaging capacity worldwide. The company is considering a new manufacturing campus in Texas that could involve tens of billions of dollars in investment and multiple fabrication plants, Bloomberg reported Thursday. Each potential fab could cost at least $20 billion. However, discussions remain at an early stage. The stock also received support after Elon Musk confirmed early-stage talks with Taiwan Semiconductor about a possible role in his planned Texas-based Terafab semiconductor project. Taiwan Semiconductor shares have gained almost 60% in 2026 as global AI infrastructure spending drives demand for its advanced chips and contract manufacturing services. The stock is trading nearly 2% higher in Monday’s premarket session as it extends its longer-term uptrend and pushes into breakout territory. Nasdaq futures are down 0.11%, while S&P 500 futures have slipped 0.04%. TSM is also pushing above its previous 52-week high. A breakout into new-high territory can attract momentum traders as investors look for the uptrend to continue. AI Demand Pushes Taiwan Semiconductor To Add Capacity North American customers generate more than 75% of Taiwan Semiconductor’s wafer revenue. NVIDIA Corp. NVDA and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. AMD are among the companies placing large orders for advanced manufacturing. Deputy Co-Chief Operating Officer Cliff Hou said Taiwan Semiconductor has roughly doubled its planned equipment purchases over the past year to keep pace with demand. The company has already committed $265 billion to its Arizona operations. It is also pursuing projects in Japan and Germany while holding discussions with Singapore officials. Counterpoint Calls Taiwan Semiconductor AI’s ‘Central Beneficiary’ Counterpoint Research sees Taiwan Semiconductor as the biggest beneficiary of the AI semiconductor boom. Taiwan Semiconductor’s second-quarter revenue rose 34% year over year and 12% sequentially to $40.2 billion. Its share of the Foundry 2.0 market increased to roughly 42% from 38% in 2025. Counterpoint expects full-year 2026 revenue to grow about 43%, with growth approaching 50% in the second half. Associate Director Brady Wang called Taiwan Semiconductor the “central beneficiary” of expanding AI investment. S&P Says Taiwan Semiconductor Could Weather An AI Slowdown Meanwhile, S&P Global Ratings expects hyperscaler AI spending to reach $1.5 trillion by 2028 and sees Taiwan Semiconductor as relatively resilient if spending slows. S&P said Taiwan Semiconductor’s technology leadership and diversified end markets should help protect pricing and margins. The ratings firm expects profitability and cash generation to remain above 2026 levels even under a weaker AI spending scenario. The potential Texas investment partly depends on an extension of a 35% U.S. advanced-manufacturing tax credit that is set to expire at the end of 2026. Despite expanding overseas, Taiwan Semiconductor plans to keep development of its most advanced chipmaking technology in Taiwan. Taiwan Semiconductor said, “We have no comment on market rumors.” Taiwan Semiconductor is scheduled to report earnings on Oct. 15. Wall Street expects earnings of $4.45 per share, up from $2.92 a year earlier. Revenue is expected to reach $45.54 billion, compared with $33.10 billion in the year-ago period. The stock trades at a price-to-earnings ratio of about 35.3, reflecting a premium valuation. TSM carries a Buy consensus rating with an average price forecast of $547.38. title: Did Halloween Already Happen in Colorado? - Retro 102.5
content: October is less than a week in, and many are excited about getting ready for Halloween. Decorations are going up in yards across the state, on balconies, and many people are getting ready for the month ahead. Halloween movies are on television, kids are wearing their costumes around the house, and many adults have begun testing the candy to make sure it is good this year. While most would assume Halloween season is ramping up, you would have a hard time guessing that by walking into certain stores. Did Halloween already take place in Colorado, and residents forgot to be told it happened already? Have you been into Costco recently? If the answer is yes, what holiday mood did the store put you in? The answer likely isn't Halloween, and during October shouldn't it be? This is the time of year when Halloween is the focal point, but as many stores have been doing through the years, they no longer respect the current season and instead are focusing on the next holiday and trying to beat their competitors to getting out their decor. Costco currently has rows of Christmas decorations, advent calendars, wrapping paper, and great gift ideas. While some have begun their holiday shopping, should Halloween be swept under the rug this soon, when the holiday is still weeks away from happening? Far too many stores are moving from one holiday to another so soon that they neglect the one that is currently in season. Not everyone is ready to move on when trunk-or-treats have not started yet, pumpkin patches only recently opened, and many do not have their costumes yet or even know what they are going to be this year. While it makes sense from a business perspective to be the first to get out holiday decorations, is now the right time to go all in on Christmas? There is nothing wrong with having a mix of Christmas and Halloween. But to fully eliminate Halloween and have more Christmas seems absurd. When do you think is the right time to go all in on Christmas? Is it the week of Halloween when most things are bought? Is it the day after Halloween? Or are you traditional and believe it should be the week of or day after Thanksgiving?

title: New Record High in TSM Stock, Eyeing $500 as TSMC Explores Role in Musk TeraFab - FXLeaders
content: TSM stock has climbed to fresh record highs above $480 as strong NVIDIA results reinforce semiconductor demand and potential TSMC involvement in Elon Musk’s TeraFab adds another growth catalyst. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing shares have extended their rally above $480, surpassing the previous record from June and moving toward the psychologically important $500 level. The latest momentum comes as investors assess the potential for TSMC to participate in Elon Musk’s $16.8 billion TeraFab project in Texas. Musk has confirmed that discussions with TSMC are underway, although he indicated that negotiations remain at an early stage. Intel was previously identified as a manufacturing partner after joining the project in April, with its 14A process technology selected for the proposed facility. However, reports that TSMC is exploring a role could create an additional opportunity for the world’s largest advanced-chip foundry. The potential partnership follows reports that TSMC is considering expanding its manufacturing presence in Texas after developing its Arizona operations. Reports have suggested TSMC could eventually establish multiple advanced fabs in Texas. One possibility would involve TSMC owning and operating a new facility while SpaceX participates through equity investment or guaranteed purchase agreements. The TeraFab concept was initially proposed by Musk in 2025 after he argued that existing semiconductor supply would not be sufficient for Tesla’s long-term requirements. In March 2026, Musk announced plans for a semiconductor facility in Austin, Texas, positioned near Tesla’s headquarters and intended as a joint venture between Tesla and SpaceX. Intel subsequently joined the project, but the potential involvement of TSMC could broaden the manufacturing strategy. NVIDIA’s latest results provide another major catalyst for TSM stock. NVIDIA operates a fabless model, designing its processors while relying on external manufacturers such as TSMC for production. TSMC manufactures the majority of NVIDIA’s most advanced chips, meaning continued growth in GPU demand directly supports demand for TSMC’s leading-edge manufacturing capacity. Strong NVIDIA revenue and expectations for continued infrastructure spending therefore reinforce the broader semiconductor cycle. Unlike NVIDIA, which must justify extremely high growth expectations, TSMC can benefit from demand generated by multiple customers across the semiconductor industry. TSM stock was already showing strong momentum before NVIDIA released its results, and the move above $487 suggests investors are increasingly positioning for continued growth in advanced semiconductor demand. The company’s manufacturing leadership gives it a central role in the production of high-end chips used by major technology companies. The same spending boom supporting TSM stock also creates longer-term risks. Semiconductor companies are committing enormous amounts of capital to computing infrastructure, advanced processors and new manufacturing facilities. For TSMC, this creates opportunities for higher revenue and utilization, but expectations are becoming increasingly elevated. If NVIDIA’s growth slows or customers reduce infrastructure spending, semiconductor orders could eventually weaken. There is also a risk that aggressive investment creates excess capacity if supply expands faster than underlying demand. For now, buyers remain firmly in control as TSM stock trades above $480 and approaches the $500 psychological level. A sustained breakout above $500 could reinforce the broader uptrend, while failure to hold the new record zone could trigger profit-taking. With potential TeraFab involvement and strong NVIDIA-driven demand supporting the story, TSMC remains positioned to benefit from the semiconductor investment cycle. However, the increasingly aggressive spending environment means investors will need to watch both demand growth and capacity expansion closely.
